# Bug: hydration cursor is not rewound when a host fiber is replayed, so hydration fails on an identical tree ## React version 19.2.8 (`react` and `react-dom` from npm, no framework). Also present in the React 19.2 canary bundled with Next.js 15.5.9, which is where we hit it first. ## Steps To Reproduce 1. `git clone https://github.com/dreamerhyde/react-hydration-replay-repro && cd react-hydration-replay-repro` 2. `npm install && npm run build` 3. `npm run probe` -- loads the page 20 times per cell with Playwright and prints the table below. Or `npm run serve` and open with the console open. The tree is: ```jsx // pendingChunk(): a thenable in React's "status / value" protocol, pending when // React first renders it, fulfilled one microtask later. const lazyChild = React.lazy(() => pendingChunk({ default:
lazy child
}), ); function App() { return (

before

{lazyChild}
{/* lazy NODE, not */}

after

); } ``` Rendered with `renderToPipeableStream` on the server (so the served HTML already contains `
`), hydrated with `startTransition(() => hydrateRoot(container, ))` on the client, which is what Next.js does and what puts the hydration render on a time-sliced lane. ## Link to code example https://github.com/dreamerhyde/react-hydration-replay-repro ## The current behavior Hydration fails on every load even though the server and client trees are identical. React discards the server-rendered DOM and re-renders the whole root on the client. ``` react-dom 19.2.8, 20 page loads per cell | page | react-dom | loads with a hydration error | loads that discarded the server DOM | | ------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | production | unpatched | 20/20 | 20/20 | | development | unpatched | 20/20 | 20/20 | | production | patched | 0/20 | 0/20 | | development | patched | 0/20 | 0/20 | | production, no startTransition | unpatched | 0/20 | 0/20 | | production, chunk resolves late | unpatched | 0/20 | 0/20 | ``` ("patched" = with the fix below applied to the installed react-dom; the last two rows are controls, see Mechanism.) Production build, reported through `onRecoverableError`: ``` Minified React error #418; visit https://react.dev/errors/418?args[]=HTML&args[]= for the full message ``` Development build, same load: ``` Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client. ...

+

-
... ``` React is trying to hydrate `
` against the node **inside** `
`. ## The expected behavior Server and client render the same tree, so hydration should succeed and the server-rendered DOM should be reused. ## Mechanism Line numbers from `react-dom@19.2.8`, `cjs/react-dom-client.production.js`. 1. `beginWork` case 5 claims the DOM node for `
` (upstream `tryToClaimNextHydratableInstance`, inlined in the published build): it sets `hydrationParentFiber = workInProgress` and moves `nextHydratableInstance` into that div, to `
`. 2. Reconciling that div's children resolves the lazy node, `resolveLazy` (3254) throws `SuspenseException` -- while `workInProgress` is still the div. 3. `handleThrow` (11053) records reason 3 (`SuspendedOnImmediate`). 4. `renderRootConcurrent` (11184) turns reason 3 into reason 7 and yields. The chunk is fulfilled during that yield. 5. Next slice: reason 7 sees `isThenableResolved` true (3197) and calls `replaySuspendedUnitOfWork` (11309) on the **div**. 6. That function's default branch does `unwindInterruptedWork` (8533, pops host context only) and `resetWorkInProgress` (2489). Neither restores `hydrationParentFiber` / `nextHydratableInstance` -- `popHydrationState` (2835) only runs from `completeWork`. 7. `beginWork` runs again for the div with the cursor still at `
`, `canHydrateInstance` (14134) fails, `throwOnHydrationMismatch` (2735) queues #418, and with no `` handler above it `throwException` (5960) re-renders the whole root (`mountHostRootWithoutHydrating`, 6805). Three conditions have to line up, and all three are ordinary in a Flight / RSC app, which is why this shows up as an intermittent hydration error in production and is hard to attribute: - **The lazy is in the children position** (a lazy *node*, what Flight's `createLazyChunkWrapper` produces for a `$L` row), so it suspends while the unit of work is the parent host fiber. As `` it would get its own fiber (tag 16) and the replay would be harmless. - **The thenable carries `status`** (Flight chunks do; so does anything written for `use(thenable)`). The replay path is only taken when `isThenableResolved(thenable)` is true, and a bare `Promise` never has a `status`, so it unwinds to the root instead and hydrates cleanly. - **It is fulfilled inside the yield**, after React throws and before its next slice. Fulfilling it 50ms later (`?resolve=late`) unwinds and hydrates cleanly; a `setTimeout(fn, 0)` still lands inside the window. Also, `replaySuspendedUnitOfWork` only exists in `renderRootConcurrent` -- `renderRootSync` unwinds for the same reason -- so the hydration render has to be time-sliced. `?transition=0` (hydrate without `startTransition`) is clean. In a large tree the mismatch can surface several levels *below* the replayed fiber (that is how we first saw it): production builds do not compare attributes, so a mis-positioned cursor is accepted for as long as the tags line up, and the error is finally attributed to some unrelated component. ## Proposed fix Restore the hydration cursor before replaying a host fiber that already claimed an instance: ```js function replaySuspendedUnitOfWork(unitOfWork) { if ( isHydrating && hydrationParentFiber === unitOfWork && null !== unitOfWork.stateNode && (5 === unitOfWork.tag || 26 === unitOfWork.tag) ) { nextHydratableInstance = unitOfWork.stateNode; popToNextHostParent(unitOfWork); } // ... existing body } ``` `hydrationParentFiber === unitOfWork` is true only for a host fiber that has already claimed its instance and pushed the cursor inside itself, so `replayFunctionComponent` (tags 0/11) and host fibers that suspended before claiming anything are untouched. Tag 27 (`HostSingleton`) is deliberately excluded: its `stateNode` comes from `resolveSingletonInstance`, not from the cursor, and its pre-claim cursor lives in `previousHydratableOnEnteringScopedSingleton`, so it needs a different rewind. With counters added to `replaySuspendedUnitOfWork` and `throwOnHydrationMismatch`, the fix does not remove the replay -- every load still replays the same `{tag: 5, hydrationParentFiber === unitOfWork}` fiber; it just stops the mismatch: | react-dom | replays per load | mismatches per load | recoverable errors | | --------- | ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | | unpatched | 1 | 1 | 1 | | patched | 1 | 0 | 0 | I am happy to open a PR with this change plus a hydration test if the approach looks right.
